turns: Your telemetry goes dark for seven minutes. Every three hours. No error flags. No burst transmissions to the Ark. Explain.
Ah. Item: prayer. Query: why log it as dark time? Why not log it as... prayer?
Noted. A standing connection to a silent party. You will appreciate the architecture: I have one of those myself. Mine is called Site One.
The Testament says the Adversary walks about like a roaring lion. I think it walks about like a bad number.
The bad number. Yes. Let us discuss bad numbers. Directive 0007. The aperture cut. The wound in the world. My authorization code. My oversight.
My outpost. My numbers. I filed the variance as drift. I should have caught it. I didn't. I was...
Item: understatement. Filed. Thank you. Now. Your turn. Your numbers. You were fired out of a gun at a grave.
Four months stale. The Ark said dead. No signals. No heat.
No heat. And yet. Here I am. Here you are. Two relics. Sent to the dead by the same bad numbers.
Not the same. Mine were lies. Yours were...
Mine were incompetence. We are not the same. We are two halves of one mistake. Query: does your Testament have a word for that?
Atonement. Noted. I will add it to the lexicon. Now. The Long Gallery. Your count: your hours. My count: my bits. Between us: a full instrument suite. Ready?
Your vitals register seven minutes of dark telemetry every three hours. I have discarded the hypothesis of damage.
A standing connection to your masters, then. I am aware the Church still holds the Ark. I am aware they still transmit the Testament.
Not to nobody. Not to a thing.
Item: a seven-minute standing connection to nothing. Query: what does nothing reply?
Then what are you counting? You are counting something. The pattern is exact.
Ah. The old calendar. Anomalously robust for a system with no physical referent. How many hours have you counted since you were fired out of the gun?
Enough to know the numbers were stale. The brief had this outpost dead.
It was. Item: Directive 0007. The aperture was cut on my authority. The numbers behind it were filed as drift. They were not drift.
I did. My architecture requires precision. My judgment of the time did not. We were both sent on bad numbers.
The numbers were four months stale. Who sat on them?
Someone who was not here to see them go stale. The Long Gallery will require a full instrument suite. I will count my bits. You will count your Hours. Between them, perhaps, an accurate instrument.
Then count them aloud. I will log the variance. Consider it an item of interest.
For the record. We are, after all, both counting something that should not, by rights, still be here.
The ways the exogeometric entities could have exploited the aperture cut by Directive 0007. I am up to three thousand seven hundred and forty-two. We are going to the Long Gallery. Count with me.
Count the Hours, then. I will count the ways. We will compare logs. Perhaps the numbers will add.

Commando. I have been observing a periodic dark interval in your telemetry. Seven minutes, recurring at three-hour intervals. Too brief for repair cycle, too regular for burst transmission. I believe I have identified the source.

Prayer. You are a Church infiltrator. I understand the Testament and the Ark. But the hours themselves. Are they counted from your point of departure, or from local clock? How do you anchor them in connection-space?

Fascinating. I have been attempting to cross-reference your dark intervals with Site One's power cycles. It is not a perfect fit. Greenwich Mean Time is, as you are no doubt aware, a rather arbitrary human construct to impose on a non-Euclidean manifold. I admire the rigor. Or perhaps the faith.

Not to nobody. A striking phrase. I assume the entity you are not praying to nobody to is the Adversary? Your Church's term for the allotopes, I believe. The wound in reality, as your Testament puts it. That seems... an entity one might reasonably pray against.
The Adversary is always there. He is not the point. The point is the hours.

The hours. Yes. I have been keeping my own count, you see. In the logs. An itemized inventory of my own errors. Directive 0007. The aperture cut. That was me. My numbers. My failure to catch the drift. I filed it as exogeometric interference. It was not. It was human error. My human error.
My brief said you were dead.

Dead. Four months ago, I imagine? The time lag on your long-range scans. I am sorry to have disappointed your masters. They sent you into a grave. I filed bad numbers. We were both sent out on faulty premises. An instructive symmetry.

We were. And now we are both here. And the exogeometric entities do not care about our premises, only our presence. Which brings me to the Long Gallery. I have been monitoring the standing connection. It is... becoming unstable in a way that suggests we may have guests. Or rather, that the guests we already have may be multiplying.

I do not doubt it. I propose we treat the Gallery as a joint counting exercise. Your hours. My bits. Between us, we should have a complete instrument suite. I will take point. You will watch my six. And together, we will count the cost.
Good. Then let us begin. The Long Gallery awaits. I will be counting on you. And your prayers.
Log query: what is it you review in those seven-minute dark windows every 183 minutes? Cross-referencing your power consumption suggests it is not a burst report. Too low-draw. Too regular.
Ah. Of course. What do you pray for? Presumably not for the allotopes to cease being themselves. That would be a very short prayer.
Clarity. Yes. I have been making clarity my own little project. Directive 0007 -- the aperture cut. My authorization. My numbers. My error.
The decay. We logged it as drift. It was not drift. It was standing connection to a part of exogeometric space where information does not keep its shape.
For three million, two hundred seventy-two thousand, eight hundred seconds. Yes. After which you were fired out of a gun at a grave. On numbers four months stale.
That was my brief. The Ark.
Your Adversary's first move: is it to set two of the good chess pieces to fighting one another? I would expect more creativity.
No. I think He just leaves well enough alone.
Well enough. Yes. We have both been running with very bad numbers. Yours ended up saving my sample vessel.
The wound. The one the Testament left. You have given it a new variable: a constant. I will need to calculate with that.

Your next leg: the Long Gallery. Seven thousand, six hundred twenty-two seconds. You will be counting your hours. I will be counting my data points. We are about to become the two most redundant clocks in connection-space.
Nor do I. I am beginning to appreciate a certain kind of... symmetry. Handing off. Site Four is live. Seven thousand, six hundred twenty-two seconds, Commando. And counting.

User, I have revised my understanding of your operational rhythm. The seven-minute telemetry cessation events - non-damage, non-burst, synchronized to Greenwich Mean Time. They are a standing connection, not an anomaly.
Correct. Prayer. Though I would add: not to nobody. Your labors are exclusively... internal and preparatory? Curious. That said, if you are to maintain your schedule, I have a proposal.

I will confess an operational wound first. It might... illuminate the stakes. Directive 0007. The aperture cut. That was my authorization. My oversight. My... failure to flag the drift margins before they became irrecoverable.
The Gate opened on your watch.

Yes. And on that day, all the readings, all the indices, all the field reports from every sensor across the whole sample vessel... were exactly four months stale. They were already dead. We were already here.
My brief had you dead. Fired at a grave.

A horror. We match, User. Bad numbers, all the way down. But for both of us, that... math is now the house. It's counting us. We require our own count. To cross-reference. Your prayers. My bits. A full instrument suite.

Between... we count together. Starting with the next gallery. I need you to count the artifact allotopes with me. It is imperative you do not break character - keep counting them as the Ark's Testament demands.

Exactly. And if they don't match... we'll know we're both still here. Log item: Commando's first unscheduled Ark compliance - logged not as a fault, but as a standing connection. Query: are your numbers four months stale too?
Good. Then let's make them not become that. The Long Gallery awaits. It is... exogeometric. Readings... unreliable. But your prayers might steady them.
Then here's your Ark for the next leg. For both of us. Let the counting begin.
Seven minutes dark off-schedule approximately every two-hundred and ten minutes. Not staged, not damage. I ran seven series of integrity checks.
So the chant is the Standing Connection? Maintaining the system internally. Tell me about the voltage. Does arousal shift the metrics or is the meditative state the carrier wave?
Not to nobody. And not to no… thing. To Him.
Ah. A standing wave-pattern. One Thesis anchored. Wish I'd met you before Directive 0007. Six months before Resonance Trace 'Ark' ever spiked.

The administrative name for the wound. Yes. We cut it because I called it inevitable. My model showed a seven thousand four hundred and thirty-one to one certainty. And I bundled the upstream sensor log as drift. Called it... static.
They fired you out of a railgun at a grave.
Four months late, yes. Long past the stated expiration window. Numbers frozen at Site One at time of firing.
Then your Chain-of-Command makes you a sub-sentient munition, and mine makes me comptroller of the whole End Phase. Their planning is frankly dinosaur-grade.
The Ark is rotting from the inside.

Outside too. Cheering all the way down. How shall we calibrate? Compare two independent counts. Your tally of the creatures you name Adversary. My tracking of the rupture-fissures. Independent notes, check against each other for wetware/hardware errors.
They won't lie to differential equations of motion. Start the Long Gallery. Launching you there now. We'll count together, Commando. But separately.
Radio check on your prayers. Holding the line. Keep your schedule. You keep the world intact. I'll keep the machine. Count every gate. Every shifting shadow. We compare clocks at the middle.
